crop._wasNotFromAppFrame: 🔴 RETRACTED 2026-08-27, and it was wrong in the direction that matters. This key used to read 'DELIBERATELY NOT `fromAppFrame` … y=97 is BELOW the iframe's top on purpose, because it also clips the app's OWN partially-visible buzz bar'. MEASURED live on this app's own page, booted through its ready gate: the iframe top is 141, the rewards banner occupies rows 68..104 and the breadcrumb bar 105..138 — so y=97 was 44px ABOVE the iframe, INSIDE the banner, and the shipped crop's top rows were host page chrome, not app. It clipped nothing of the app's own. 🔴 THE INTENT WAS RIGHT AND ONLY THE NUMBER WAS WRONG: the app's buzz chip sits at rows 161..181, inside the app header band 141..203 whose divider is at 204, so the crop must start at 205 — which is 64 BELOW the iframe top. That offset is non-negative, so `fromAppFrame` is not merely permitted here, it is REQUIRED: sensei is on the same apps/run/<slug> shell as every other app, the banner moves it ~36px (37 is the banner's own height, rows 68..104; the resulting SHIFT measured 36 — #1316 pinned 194->230, and conflating the two is what round 2 caught), and an absolute rect is wrong in one of the two layouts BY CONSTRUCTION. sensei was never a legitimate absolute-form case — it was an unfixed instance of the defect talos#1316 fixed for the other two apps.
crop._measured: 2026-08-27, banner PRESENT, viewport 1709x1255, app-frame top=141, bottom gap=64 (read off the run's own probe answer, APPFRAME_RECT:141,64,-1,1709,1255, taken by capture.sh immediately after the capture so the pair is matched and frame.py's scale guard validated it). y=64 resolves to abs 205 — one row below the app header's divider at 204, which is what excludes the app's own buzz chip at rows 161..181. h=982 ends at abs 1187, 4px inside the iframe's lower edge at 1191, just under the model/temperature bar. 🔴 THE RENDERED ASSET'S FRAMING CHANGES, and it is worth knowing before a re-shoot: `render` fits-inside then pads, so the old 1694x1090 became 1200x772 (3px of letterbox) and 1694x982 becomes 1200x696 — 41px of flat background top and bottom, 10.5% of the canvas. That is the cost of dropping 108 rows from the top — and be precise about WHAT they are, because '108 rows of host chrome' was wrong: only ~44 are host (97..139, banner tail + breadcrumb). The other 64 are the app's OWN header band (141..204), dropped deliberately because it carries the operator's buzz chip. w=1694. 🔴 ITS OLD JUSTIFICATION WAS WRONG AND THE TRADE IS REAL, so state both: it said 'drops the right-edge scrollbar', and there IS no scrollbar in this crop's rows (2 non-bg px per column at x>=1691). What 1694 actually keeps is the floating SUPPORT WIDGET at x1643..1690 / y1149..1189, host furniture position-fixed OVER the iframe and exactly what `right: 70` excludes on a DETECTED crop — clipped here at the crop's bottom edge. It is kept because it CANNOT be excluded without losing app content, measured: the app's own Send button occupies columns 1609..1690 at y1078..1118 — BOTH right edges are at 1690, so the two SHARE COLUMNS and any `w` at or below 1643 clips Send (tried 1639 and rendered it: Send becomes a bare 'S'). They are in different ROWS, but that does not help either: the only height that drops the widget ends at 1148, which also drops the model/temp control bar at 1157..1166. Keeping a small corner widget beats clipping the app's primary control or its settings row. 🔴 Supersedes the 2026-08-15 reading (y=97 h=1090), which put the crop's top 44 rows in host page chrome. Verify by eye after any re-shoot. 🔴 AND THE LIMIT THIS RECT HAS, which the anchored form does NOT remove: sensei is the FIRST HEIGHT-RESPONSIVE adopter. Its layout is header / flex-1 main / BOTTOM-ANCHORED control bar (full-width divider at abs 1133, model+temp+max-tokens at 1157..1166), so the app's bottom furniture tracks the IFRAME'S LOWER edge, not its top. The banner shortens the iframe from the top with the viewport fixed, so in the banner-ABSENT layout the iframe is ~36px TALLER and this top-anchored, fixed-height rect ends ~36px short — DROPPING the control bar it is measured to end just under — not clipping it: the crop would resolve to abs 168..1150 while the bar sits at 1157..1166, wholly outside. What gets CLIPPED in that layout is the support widget at 1149..1189, so the keep-the-widget trade below does not even apply there. 🔴 SILENTLY: the iframe-bottom bound does not fire, because ending EARLY is not running past the edge. So `one rect is right in both banner layouts` is TRUE for a top-aligned app and only PARTLY true here — the top edge tracks perfectly in both, the bottom edge is right in the layout it was measured in. It is still strictly better than the absolute rect it replaced, which was wrong at BOTH edges in the other layout. CLOSING CONDITION: shoot sensei with the banner ABSENT and re-measure; if the control bar is clipped, either drop it from the shot or give the form a bottom anchor. Not attempted here — no banner-absent capture exists.
crop._comment: 🔴 sensei is FULL-BLEED — session sidebar + chat pane fill the frame edge to edge — so content-DETECTION cannot work here: it found the whole band and `full_frame` refused at 100% x 98.1%, at every band setting tried. The gate was right (a detected box that fills the band IS furniture-shaped), so the crop is DECLARED. It is NOT absolute: `yFrom: appFrame` anchors `y` to the app iframe's top edge, the one edge the conditional rewards banner moves, so the TOP edge is correct in both banner layouts; x/w/h stay absolute. 🔴 The BOTTOM edge is not — see `_measured`: this app is height-responsive and a fixed `h` cannot track both layouts. `rect` bypasses detection, not the gates: it is still checked for lying inside the frame, a 128px floor per axis, for not being the whole frame, and — because it is frame-relative — for not running past the IFRAME's own lower edge. The identical-box check is inert for any declared rect, so verify by eye.

_selectors: Discovered live 2026-08-15 by the opencode browser-agent, and PARTLY WRONG — see `_bootVsPopulated`. Prefer the data-testid forms: the React-generated ids seen alongside them (#ci-textarea-_r_0_, #ci-select-_r_1_) embed a render counter and are NOT stable across loads.
_bootVsPopulated: 🔴 THE 2026-08-15 DISCOVERY PASS RAN AGAINST A POPULATED CHAT, AND EVERY SELECTOR IT TOOK FROM THAT SCREEN IS ABSENT AT BOOT. Measured live 2026-08-18 on a genuinely foregrounded tab: the ready gate exited 11 with APPBOOT_ABSENT reading `chat-input` — the app had booted past `app-loading` and the anchor simply does not exist yet. Sensei's booted-but-idle screen renders NO textarea at all; `chat-input` appears only after a session is started. The text `Ask me about AI models` is likewise NOT in the DOM (hasAskMe:false, whole body 250 chars). Testids actually present at boot: session-list, settings-bar, new-session-button, start-chat-button, buzz-balance, settings-button, model-selector, temperature-slider, max-tokens-slider. 🔴 TWO OF THOSE ARE NOW STALE, and the list is kept as the 2026-08-18 READING rather than silently corrected, because it is evidence: `open-research` was removed with the Research panel (clawgate #434, 2026-08-30) and `buzz-balance` was removed in sensei 0.1.5 — so this list is a snapshot, not a contract, and anything load-bearing must be re-measured live rather than read off it. THE LESSON, which is not sensei-specific: an anchor discovered in a POPULATED state is not a boot anchor. Discover against a fresh load, or the ready gate you add to stop boot races becomes a boot race of its own.
_notShootable: 🔴 RETRACTED 2026-08-30 — and this time it is the OBSERVATION itself, not just its explanation. This key used to say there is NO state showing a real answer, and that an answer screenshot 'can only be produced by a human pressing Enter with the tab focused'. MEASURED FALSE: a SYNTHETIC in-frame click on button[data-testid=send-button], which the bridge itself reported as trusted:false, SUBMITTED FOR REAL — a user bubble rendered and a Buzz-spending reply completed, citing real models. An earlier edit the same day had already retracted the CAUSE ('the spend path rejects untrusted events' — there is no isTrusted/userActivation check anywhere on that path). Both halves are retired; do not re-derive either. 🔴 THE OPERATIONAL RULE IS UNCHANGED, BUT ITS REASON IS NOW THE ONLY ONE LEFT: submitting SPENDS BUZZ. Do NOT add a capture state that sends. The prohibition is ECONOMIC, not mechanical. 🔴 AND THE 'A SEND IS SLOW' WARNING THIS KEY CARRIED FOR A FEW HOURS ON 2026-08-30 WAS WRONG — IT MEASURED THE INSTRUMENT, NOT THE APP. It claimed ~190 characters in ~9 minutes, still unfinished, and concluded a capture state waiting on an answer 'would time out even though nothing is broken'. The real mechanism: the reply is fetched COMPLETE and already moderated (orchestrator-bridge.ts: 'NON-STREAMING BY CONSTRUCTION' — a partial reply cannot be scanned), then the CLIENT animates it with simulateStreaming at ONE WORD PER setTimeout(20ms) — about 2 seconds for a whole answer. Chrome throttles setTimeout in a HIDDEN tab, and every agent-driven send runs in one, so the typewriter crawls to a standstill while the answer already sits in memory, released. 🔴 THE CURE IS ONE CALL, NOT A LONGER TIMEOUT: `browser wake` the TAB. Measured control — stalled at 105 chars for 3 minutes, then wake, then 726 chars and COMPLETE within 6 seconds. So an answer state IS shootable given a wake; what is forbidden is the SEND that pays for it. Generalises past sensei: any block that animates text client-side will look hung in a background tab, and the hang is your tab, not their app.

ready._comment: the session sidebar — structural, and present in BOTH the empty and the populated state (measured live 2026-08-18). `settings-bar` is the equivalent alternative. Do NOT use `chat-input` (absent until a session exists — it is what made this gate exit 11) and do NOT use `start-chat-button` (it disappears once a chat exists, so it would pass on a fresh profile and fail on a used one).
